questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

questions.questionText: After hyperinflation, the Zimbabwe dollar was no longer used and instead the country used US dollars. A coin collector in Europe bought an old Zimbabwe 100 trillion dollar note at an auction in the hope that it would later become rare and increase in value. If that happened, which function of money would the Zimbabwe dollar note fulfil?

options.A: a generally accepted means of payment

questions.questionText: In 2009, demand for second-hand used cars in Venezuela increased. What could have explained this?

options.A: a decrease in the number of Venezuelans passing their driving test
options.B: a decrease in the price of public transport
options.C: an increase in restrictions on new cars imported into Venezuela
options.D: an increase in the domestic production of cars

questions.questionText: The price elasticity of demand for a product is unitary for all price ranges. What will be the effect of an increase in its price?

options.A: an equal proportionate decrease in the amount demanded
options.B: an equal proportionate decrease in expenditure on the product
options.C: an increase in the product’s percentage of total consumer expenditure
options.D: no change in the amount of the product demanded

questions.questionText: In which case is the price system not a possible method of allocating resources?

options.A: in the distribution of foodstuff among the population
options.B: in the hiring of workers by employers
options.C: in the ownership of land for agricultural use
options.D: in the provision of public goods by the government

questions.questionText: A town council estimated the costs and benefits of operating a bus service in 2010 and 2011. These are shown in the table. 2010 2011 $000 $000 private costs 2000 2200 external costs 500 900 private benefits 1500 2300 external benefits 1000 800 What can be concluded from the table?

options.A: Between 2010 and 2011, social costs fell and social benefits rose.
options.B: Between 2010 and 2011, social costs rose and social benefits fell.
options.C: In both years, positive externalities exceeded negative externalities.
options.D: In both years, social costs equalled social benefits.

questions.questionText: A cost-benefit analysis concludes that a nuclear power station project might be socially worthwhile, although it will take 10 years to bring into operation. Why might a government decide not to undertake the project?

options.A: Cost-benefit analysis has no method for valuing the long-term impact of a project.
options.B: Cost-benefit analysis is only suitable for private sector projects.
options.C: The government believes that the project has too high an opportunity cost.
options.D: The government’s policy is to restrict the extent of the market system.

questions.questionText: A good is more likely to be supplied by the government rather than a private company if it is

options.A: excludable and non-rival.

questions.questionText: A government fixes a maximum price for a product in order to increase its consumption. What would be the likely outcome of such a policy?

options.A: Consumption will fall if the maximum price is above the current equilibrium price.
options.B: Consumption will rise if the maximum price is below the current equilibrium price.
options.C: Production will fall if the maximum price is above the current equilibrium price.
options.D: Production will fall if the maximum price is below the current equilibrium price.

options.C: a credit in the financial account uncertain in the current account
